notes: The BTS Skytrain and MRT are the fastest ways to get around the city. Make taxi drivers use the meter; tuk-tuks involve haggling and are touristy. The Grab app is reliable.
Shoulders and knees must be covered in temples. Checks are strict at the Grand Palace, where sarongs are sold but expensive.
November to February is the best season (28°C, dry). March to May can hit 38°C, so sightsee early and take air-conditioned breaks.
Street food is safe: pick a busy stall, and ice is fine. Pad thai costs 60-100 THB, mango sticky rice 100 THB.
Tipping is not obligatory; restaurants may add a 10% service charge. Haggling is normal in markets, not in malls.
The train from Hua Lamphong to Ayutthaya takes 1.5 hours (20-60 THB). For the floating markets, take a tour or hire a car.

transit.name: Rabbit Card
transit.why_chosen: Works on the BTS Skytrain; the MRT needs a separate token or card. You can buy both at the station.

days.theme: Grand Palace, Wat Pho and Wat Arun

stops.name: Grand Palace Bangkok
stops.tips: The royal palace and the Emerald Buddha (Wat Phra Kaew). Entry is 500 THB, shoulders and knees must be covered. Go in at 08:30 to beat the crowds.

stops.name: Wat Pho
stops.tips: A 46 m reclining Buddha and a massage school. Get a 30-minute traditional massage here (~300 THB).

stops.name: Tha Tien Pier
stops.tips: Cross the Chao Phraya on the 5 THB ferry. Wat Arun is right opposite.

stops.name: Wat Arun
stops.tips: The Temple of Dawn. Climb the steep stairs of the porcelain-covered prang for views over the river.

stops.name: Supanniga Eating Room Tha Tien
stops.tips: Thai home cooking on the riverside. Have lunch with a view of Wat Arun: moo palo (braised pork belly) and som tam (green papaya salad).

backups.name: Thipsamai Pad Thai
backups.tips: Bangkok's most famous pad thai. Queues build after 17:00, so lunchtime is calmer.

backups.name: Museum Siam
backups.tips: An interactive Thai museum next to Wat Pho. A good option for a rainy day.

stops.name: Wat Traimit
stops.tips: A 5.5-tonne golden Buddha, at the gateway to Chinatown.

stops.name: Yaowarat Road
stops.tips: Chinatown's main street: gold shops, temples and quiet side streets by day.

stops.name: Talat Noi
stops.tips: An old Chinese quarter on the riverbank, with street art, garages and cafés.

stops.name: Hua Seng Hong Yaowarat
stops.tips: A classic Chinatown Chinese restaurant. Order dim sum and goose.

stops.name: Iconsiam
stops.tips: A huge mall across the river. Eat street food on the Sook Siam floating market floor and enjoy an air-conditioned afternoon.

backups.name: Nai Ek Roll Noodle
backups.tips: Pork noodle soup on Yaowarat, a street-food classic.

backups.name: Lhong 1919
backups.tips: A restored Chinese temple and warehouse complex on the riverside. Quieter than Iconsiam.

stops.name: Jim Thompson House
stops.tips: A teak Thai house with a silk collection. Join the guided tour; the garden stays cool.

stops.name: Siam Paragon
stops.tips: Siam's giant mall. There is a food market on the lower floor, and it makes an air-conditioned break.

stops.name: Som Tam Nua Siam Square
stops.tips: Isan cuisine: som tam and fried chicken. The queue moves fast at Siam Square.

stops.name: Erawan Shrine
stops.tips: A Brahma shrine in the middle of the city, with dancers and incense.

stops.name: Lumphini Park
stops.tips: Bangkok's central park: monitor lizards, sunset and evening aerobics.

backups.name: MBK Center Food Court
backups.tips: The food court on MBK's 6th floor. Cheap and air-conditioned, an alternative to som tam.

backups.name: Benjakitti Park
backups.tips: A new wetland park, an alternative to Lumphini.

stops.name: Chatuchak Weekend Market
stops.tips: On weekends it is the world's largest market (15,000 stalls); on weekdays head to the Or Tor Kor food market. Go early, as it gets hot by midday.

stops.name: Or Tor Kor Market
stops.tips: A premium food market next to Chatuchak. Try mango sticky rice and seafood.

stops.name: Ari Neighbourhood
stops.tips: Bangkok's hipster neighbourhood, with cafés and boutiques. Take the BTS to Ari.

stops.name: Jay Fai
stops.tips: A Michelin-starred street restaurant. Try the crab omelette (~1,000 THB). Book months ahead or join the queue at 14:00.

backups.name: Baan Ying Ari
backups.tips: Thai home cooking in Ari, if you miss out on Jay Fai.

backups.name: Chatuchak Park
backups.tips: A park next to the market, with shade and a lake.

stops.name: Wat Mahathat Ayutthaya
stops.tips: 1.5 hours from Bangkok (train or minivan). See the Buddha head wrapped in tree roots in the UNESCO-listed ancient capital.

stops.name: Wat Phra Si Sanphet
stops.tips: A royal temple with three chedis (bell-shaped stupas), the symbol of Ayutthaya.

stops.name: Wat Chaiwatthanaram
stops.tips: A Khmer-style temple on the riverbank, also famous for its sunsets. Get there by bike.

stops.name: Ayutthaya Boat Noodle
stops.tips: Ayutthaya's boat noodles come in small bowls. Have 3-4.

stops.name: Ayutthaya Night Market Pier
stops.tips: A riverside market with views of the temples. The return train leaves at 17:00.

backups.name: Bang Pa-In Palace
backups.tips: A summer palace on the way back, with gardens and pavilions.

stops.name: Damnoen Saduak Floating Market
stops.tips: 1.5 hours from Bangkok. The famous floating market is less crowded at 08:00; haggle over boat hire.

stops.name: Maeklong Railway Market
stops.tips: A market on the train tracks. Check the train times (around 11:10 and 14:30).

stops.name: Amphawa Floating Market
stops.tips: A canalside market with seafood grilled on boats. It is livelier at weekends.

stops.name: Wat Bang Kung
stops.tips: A temple swallowed by a banyan tree, near Amphawa.

backups.name: Amphawa Firefly Tour
backups.tips: An evening boat tour (if you stay overnight) to see fireflies.

backups.name: Damnoen Saduak Boat Food Stall
backups.tips: Noodles and mango served from a boat at the floating market. Go here if you skip Amphawa.

stops.name: Wat Saket (Golden Mount)
stops.tips: The Golden Mount: 344 steps and 360° views of the city. It is cool in the morning.

stops.name: Bangkok Flower Market Pak Khlong Talat
stops.tips: A 24-hour flower market, with jasmine garlands and orchids.

stops.name: Baan Khanitha Sathorn
stops.tips: Classic Thai cuisine in a Thai house. A farewell lunch, air-conditioned.

stops.name: Lumphini MRT / Airport Rail Link
stops.tips: The airport train takes 30 minutes from Phaya Thai. Time to say goodbye.

backups.name: Krua Apsorn Dinso
backups.tips: Home-style dishes from the royal kitchen. Try the crab omelette.

backups.name: Wat Suthat
backups.tips: A temple with a giant swing, an alternative to the Golden Mount.
